title: Group-composition code for algebraic matrix memory
hypothesis: A compact Mirror group element code over a shared generator reaches the minimal faithful representation for cyclic group composition, preserving heldout products with fewer bytes and compute than independent matrix memories and native group indices.

world.composition: multiply group elements by adding codes mod 16; compare decoded 2x2 action matrices

fresh.release_rule: Keep fresh sealed after exact native group-code alias.

controls: shared generator plus Mirror integer code
native cyclic group element index and matrix power
success_gate: composition nRMSE <=1e-6, at least 25% fewer bytes than independent bank, and strict quality/byte/compute advantage over native group-index control.
failure_gate: FAIL if native group representation exactly matches code or compute/storage gate does not improve.

compute.operations: report table lookup versus integer modular addition and 2x2 matrix multiplication separately

boundaries: Exact finite cyclic group toy only; no learned memory or neural-network claim.
The group law and order are known; this is not group discovery.
No fresh data after exact native group-code alias.
